title: What Does Zero Trust Mean for Agentic AI?
summary: AI agents shouldn’t be trusted by default, even when they operate inside your organization. title: BIG MOVE: Neo4j Locks $100 Million as Graph AI Reshapes How Enterprises Build AI Agents
summary: Neo4j is backing over 50 Indian AI startups, even as research suggests most generative AI projects struggle to show profit. In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Ish Thukral, Vice President & General Manager for Asia-Pacific & Japan (APJ) at Neo4j. They explore how native graph databases outperform traditional relational joins, deploying GraphRAG across tier-1 Indian banks for mule account and fraud detection, acquiring GraphAware (Hume) for visual intelligence, expanding cloud partnership models across AWS, GCP, and Azure, and driving AI data sovereignty for Indian enterprises. Beyond general development, these tools are finding specific traction in areas such as data migration and cyber fraud detection. By identifying these high-value use cases, Neo4j is positioning its platform as an essential foundation for AI startups looking to move past the experimental phase of development. title: HUGE: US DOE Puts $215 Million Bounty on Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computer by 2028
summary: The Department of Energy has launched the Quantum Genesis Q competition to build fault-tolerant quantum computers. The U.S. government is committing $215 million to accelerate the development of practical quantum machines. This initiative focuses on companies capable of demonstrating 100 logical qubits that can execute millions of fault-tolerant operations, marking a shift toward error-corrected systems rather than simple physical qubit counts. To ensure hardware claims are legitimate, the program includes a $45 million validation test bed at national laboratories. title: RAG Just Became a Trainable Neural Graph (WikiFM)
summary: Are your agentic RAG pipelines bottlenecked by sparse knowledge graphs that ruthlessly shred dense contextual semantics into rigid triples? title: The Chip Built for Agentic AI Inference, with SambaNova's Anton McGonnell (Ep. 1028)
summary: In Episode #1028, Anton McGonnell (VP of Product at SambaNova) joins @JonKrohnLearns to explain why the chips running most AI inference today were never designed for the job. Agentic AI has changed the computational profile of inference, with much larger inputs and far heavier caches feeding the token generation that follows, and that shift has exposed where GPU architecture struggles. SambaNova has raised over $2 billion to build an alternative, the reconfigurable dataflow unit, which lays a whole model out spatially across the chip rather than executing it kernel by kernel. In this episode, Anton discusses why the speed that matters is payback, and how speed and concurrency are what turn a fixed hardware cost into a six-month payback. He also walks through the trade-off every inference provider faces between speed per user and throughput per chip, what the RDU architecture changes about scaling and data center deployment, the economics of the new SN50, and why four out of five AI infrastructure leaders say they would pay a premium for faster tokens. In this episode you will learn: • (00:00:00) Introduction • (00:02:41) Why agentic AI is reshaping inference workloads • (00:08:39) How SambaNova's RDU differs from a GPU • (00:17:54) The economics of the SN50 Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/1028

title: Ai2 + the Providence Swedish Cancer Institute partner to bring AI tools to cancer data
summary: On August 27, 2026 Ai2 announced a new partnership with the Paul G. Allen Research Center (PARC) at Providence Swedish Cancer Institute to apply Ai2’s AI-powered scientific discovery platform, AutoDiscovery across cancer research datasets. This partnership represents an important milestone for AutoDiscovery as it moves beyond public research datasets into active cancer research programs at a leading oncology research center. It’s a particularly significant deployment given the high standard required for AI adoption in biomedical science, where every finding must be transparent, reproducible, and independently validated before informing future research. This event hosted at Ai2 in Seattle, presents that work and explores some of the tough issues surrounding AI deployment in the biomedical sphere.

title: Fabulous Adventures in Data Structures and Algorithms
summary:
Legendary language designer Eric Lippert guides us with a refreshing, conversational approach, providing beautifully practical examples that highlight the recurring patterns behind stubborn coding problems in his book, Fabulous Adventures in Data Structures and Algorithms.

In this session, we’ll ask these questions:
- Why do data structures and algorithms feel disconnected from real-world programming?
- How can developers reason about complexity without getting lost in notation?
- When are immutable data structures better than mutable ones?
- How can immutable stacks, queues, and deques remain efficient?
- How does memoization turn expensive algorithms into practical solutions?
- When should developers use a trie or a Directed Acyclic Word Graph?
- How can programmers control the combinatorial explosion of possible solutions?
- When is backtracking the right strategy for a search problem?
- Why can a greedy algorithm succeed without exploring every possibility?
- How can graph-coloring problems teach practical constraint solving?
- What do unification and anti-unification solve in real applications?
- Can category theory and monads genuinely improve everyday code?
- How can developers model randomness without creating untestable programs?
- How does Bayes’ theorem help software reason under uncertainty?
- How can sampling and Markov processes solve problems that resist exact computation?

title:
Don’t let your portfolio outsmart you.

If AI helped build your project, be ready to explain the cod
summary: Don’t let your portfolio outsmart you. If AI helped build your project, be ready to explain the code in an interview. Start with one failure case, like a user requesting someone else’s private data. Have the agent write a test that expects access to be denied, check that expectation yourself, then review the implementation it produces. #short

title: ALERT: UPI Charges Are Coming - But Not for You. Here's What Actually Changes
summary: Starting October 15, 2026, a 0.4% UPI MDR applies to specific merchant payments. Here is how this change impacts the market. The new framework introduces a 0.4% fee for merchant payments over 2,000 rupees, though person-to-person transfers remain entirely free. Crucially, the government mandates that merchants cannot pass these costs onto customers, protecting the end user while ensuring the financial sustainability of the UPI ecosystem. Only a small fraction of transactions—roughly 4%—are expected to be affected, as most payments fall below the threshold or qualify for exemptions. Essential sectors like fuel, telecom, and railways will see a flat 5-rupee fee for transactions over 2,000 rupees, rather than the percentage-based rate. This adjustment is designed to fund necessary infrastructure, cybersecurity, and the continued expansion of digital payments across India. summary_html:
Every agent, language model and predictive system is built on the same foundation. Get this part right and the rest of the glossary is easier.

Terms covered:
- Artificial Intelligence: systems that learn, adapt and improve from data instead of following fixed rules written by a programmer
- Machine Learning: the mechanism, where a model learns to tell fraud from non-fraud by seeing thousands of examples
- Features: the variables and attributes that tell a model what to pay attention to
- GPU: the hardware that makes training viable on text, images and video, built for thousands of calculations running at once

AI sets the vision. Machine learning is the mechanism. Features are what the model learns from. GPUs are what make it scalable.

title: How a Robot Tests an Action Before It Moves
summary: How can a robot test an action without moving? NVIDIA's Ming-Yu Liu explains how a world model predicts the outcome first. Cosmos 3 learns three abilities together: forward dynamics (what happens after an action), inverse dynamics (which action caused a change) and policy (what the robot should do next). The results in the paper show that each one helps the others. The payoff is a closed-loop simulator. Instead of setting up a thousand kitchens, developers can check a robot policy in simulation before trying it for real. Full interview: https://youtu.be/L6tLBApQN-g Learn more about Cosmos: https://nvda.ws/4cJoY1S Explore Cosmos Lab: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/cosmos-lab/cosmos3/ This video is a paid partnership with NVIDIA.

title: How Physical AI Learns Across Language, Video and Action — Ming-Yu Liu
summary: The car making a left turn at the start of this episode was never filmed. Cosmos 3 generated it. Ming-Yu Liu, who leads the Cosmos research at NVIDIA, explains how one model can describe a video, generate one, and produce robot actions. He walks Tim through the architecture. A vision language model reasons one token at a time; its weights then initialise a bidirectional diffusion generator for video, audio and action, and a shared temporal position scheme lines up signals that run at different rates. Ming-Yu treats "world model" as a set of tools, not one definition: forward dynamics, inverse dynamics and policy, trained together under a capacity limit so that each helps the others. He also explains why plentiful first-person human video carries over to robots, which have far less data of their own, and why a Cosmos model post-trained on the DROID dataset is a good starting point for pick-and-place policies. The most practical thread is testing. A neural simulator does not need accurate success rates. It only needs to rank policy A above policy B the way the real world would, so a team can narrow down which checkpoints deserve a real trial. Cosmos Dreams applies that closed-loop idea to driving and robotics, and Ming-Yu argues that humanoids around children and pets make safety matter even more than it does for cars. The conversation ends on the Super, Nano and Edge sizes (Edge targets Jetson Thor, Orin and DGX Spark) and where to find the open weights, code and data. This episode is a paid partnership with NVIDIA. title: A day in the life of a Cryogenic Systems Engineer
summary:
In August 2026, IBM successfully connected and cooled two cryogenic modules into a single operating environment: 
https://www.ibm.com/quantum/blog/modular-cryogenics
 
The achievement validates a fundamental design principle behind the IBM Quantum roadmap: Quantum computers of the future should be built as modular systems.
 
Instead of housing processors inside isolated cryostats, our architecture creates connected cryogenic cells that can be linked together while maintaining the ultra-cold temperatures required for quantum computation.
 
In this video, IBM Quantum Cryogenic Assembly Engineer Allie Lindler answers some of our most frequently asked questions about this new modular approach to housing and cooling quantum processors, including what it takes to achieve and maintain scalable, ultracold temperatures as a cryogenics specialist.

title: HISTORIC: DRDO Builds a Chip Smaller Than a Fingernail That Can Power India's Next Radar System
summary:
DRDO has developed indigenous Gallium Nitride technology, a major leap forward for India's radar and defense systems.

The Defence Research and Development Organisation has demonstrated a new 3.5x3 mm chip capable of delivering up to 30W of power. This advancement supports high-frequency operations up to X-band, providing superior power density compared to traditional silicon. By utilizing indigenous 4-inch silicon carbide wafers, the Gallium Arsenide Enabling Technology Centre in Hyderabad is now establishing limited production for these critical components.

Developing indigenous Gallium Nitride technology is a strategic move to secure India's supply chain and bypass foreign export controls. While this demonstration marks a significant milestone for defense electronics, the focus now shifts to scaling production for reliable, mass-market deployment. This capability is essential for modern electronic warfare systems, ensuring that India's semiconductor manufacturing infrastructure remains resilient and self-reliant.

title: Inside quantum optimization research
summary:
Optimization is often cited as one of quantum computing’s most promising applications. Businesses and researchers are constantly searching for better routes, schedules, allocations, and ways to allocate limited resources, meaning that a computational advantage for quantum optimization methods could deliver enormous value. Yet despite years of research, fundamental questions remain: Which optimization problems are best suited to quantum computers? And how will we know when quantum methods have truly surpassed their classical counterparts? 

 

In this episode of the Coherence Times, we’re joined by IBM’s Stefan Wörner and Stephanie Riedmüller of the Zuse Institute to explore the promise and limitations of quantum optimization. Together, they discuss the search for new quantum algorithms, the importance of benchmarking and community-driven research, and what it will take for quantum computers to deliver practical advantages for real-world optimization problems.  

Learn more about quantum computing and explore the IBM Quantum Platform → https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com 

Are you an optimization researcher? Contribute to the Quantum Optimization Benchmarking Library → https://github.com/ZIB-AOPT/QOBLIB

title: Why Voice AI Still Needs a Screen | Pavan Muddireddy
summary: Ordering food by voice alone is harder than it sounds: without a menu in front of you, you have to hold every item in your head while you decide. Pavankumar Reddy Muddireddy, who leads audio research at Mistral AI, uses that example to explain why he expects voice to sit on top of a screen rather than replace it. The screen lets you take in information quickly and gives you proof that the system did what it said. Watch the full conversation with Pavan: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ixu0H8bsCts The full episode was produced in partnership with Mistral AI. Machine Learning Street Talk

title: Speech Recognition Is Not a Solved Problem — Pavan Muddireddy
summary: Pavankumar Reddy Muddireddy leads audio research at Mistral AI. He joins Tim Scarfe for a deep technical tour of Voxtral — and explains why, after everything that has landed in the last two years, the frontier of deployed voice is still a cascade of specialised models rather than one end-to-end system. IN PARTNERSHIP WITH MISTRAL AI: --- This episode was produced in partnership with Mistral AI. Mistral AI: https://mistral.ai/ --- The conversation opens on architecture. Voxtral Chat feeds a 3B Ministral text trunk with continuous embeddings from an audio encoder, fed into the decoder as direct token input rather than through cross-attention as in Whisper, so the model can answer questions about emotion, timing and who spoke when without an intermediate transcript to lose them. The real-time model changes shape into a dual-stream decoder that consumes audio and emits text at the same time, at a configurable target delay down to 160ms, with slower streams running in parallel for anything that can afford to wait for more context. On the generation side, Pavan explains why Voxtral TTS predicts continuous latents rather than discrete codec tokens, traces the lineage from SoundStream through EnCodec to Mimi's split of semantic and acoustic codebooks, and places finite scalar quantisation and flow matching in it. Tim presses on the engineering priors underneath: why a mel spectrogram instead of the raw waveform, what noise augmentation actually buys, and the point at which acoustic overfitting becomes somebody's fine-tuning problem. Then the failure modes. Speaker diarisation is emitted autoregressively as part of the transcript rather than by a separate head, which makes streaming diarisation fragile in a particular way — less context, late speaker changes, invented extra speakers. And because the architecture commits to what it has already predicted, a single out-of-distribution mistake can compound into looping or skipped segments, which is what DPO is there to correct: the negative supervision that pre-training and SFT cannot provide. The last third is the argument Tim keeps returning to. Customers running voice agents over millions of sessions do not describe a solved problem, they describe scaffolding, with a sharp quality drop outside the top few languages. Cascades survive because each component stays separately adaptable, observable and constrainable — fine-tune the ASR for your acoustics, log what compliance demands, keep it on your own hardware. The interface has its own limit: voice alone is cognitive debt, because absorbing information and deciding in one serial audio stream is much harder than glancing at a menu. Voice becomes ubiquitous beside a screen, not instead of one. --- TIMESTAMPS: 00:00:00 Cold open: the state changed 00:00:46 Why Mistral moved into audio 00:09:27 Inside Voxtral: the trunk, the encoder and dual streams 00:20:22 Speech that works in real time 00:30:52 How a voice becomes tokens 00:39:59 Flow matching, FSQ and the new codec 00:52:51 When speech models lose the speaker 01:03:23 Correcting hallucinations with preferences 01:12:12 Controlling synthetic speech 01:20:06 Why cascades still win 01:29:25 Speech in the wild 01:33:46 Audio models as interfaces 01:37:54 Why voice still needs a screen --- REFERENCES: paper: [00:01:42] Mistral 7B https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06825 [00:09:38] Voxtral https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.13264 [00:14:41] Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision (Whisper) https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.04356 [00:19:11] Voxtral Realtime https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11298 [00:21:52] Streaming Sequence-to-Sequence Learning with Delayed Streams Modeling https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.08753 [00:30:52] Voxtral TTS https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.25551 [00:32:38] SoundStream: An End-to-End Neural Audio Codec https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.03312 [00:34:59] Flow Matching for Generative Modeling https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.02747 [00:37:03] High Fidelity Neural Audio Compression (EnCodec) https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.13438 [00:37:42] Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue (Mimi) https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.00037 [00:39:05] Finite Scalar Quantization: VQ-VAE Made Simple https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15505 [01:03:33] Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18290 benchmark: [01:15:40] ElevenLabs v3 and Flash comparison in Voxtral TTS https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.25551 dataset: [00:46:14] Mozilla Common Voice datasets https://commonvoice.mozilla.org/en/datasets organization: [00:01:24] Mistral AI https://mistral.ai/ [00:50:47] Hugging Face https://huggingface.co/

Pavankumar Reddy Muddireddy leads audio research at Mistral AI. He joins Tim Scarfe for a deep technical tour of Voxtral — and explains why, after everything that has landed in the last two years, the frontier of deployed voice is still a cascade of specialised models rather than one end-to-end system.

IN PARTNERSHIP WITH MISTRAL AI:
---
This episode was produced in partnership with Mistral AI.
Mistral AI: https://mistral.ai/
---

The conversation opens on architecture. Voxtral Chat feeds a 3B Ministral text trunk with continuous embeddings from an audio encoder, fed into the decoder as direct token input rather than through cross-attention as in Whisper, so the model can answer questions about emotion, timing and who spoke when without an intermediate transcript to lose them. The real-time model changes shape into a dual-stream decoder that consumes audio and emits text at the same time, at a configurable target delay down to 160ms, with slower streams running in parallel for anything that can afford to wait for more context.

On the generation side, Pavan explains why Voxtral TTS predicts continuous latents rather than discrete codec tokens, traces the lineage from SoundStream through EnCodec to Mimi's split of semantic and acoustic codebooks, and places finite scalar quantisation and flow matching in it. Tim presses on the engineering priors underneath: why a mel spectrogram instead of the raw waveform, what noise augmentation actually buys, and the point at which acoustic overfitting becomes somebody's fine-tuning problem. Then the failure modes. Speaker diarisation is emitted autoregressively as part of the transcript rather than by a separate head, which makes streaming diarisation fragile in a particular way — less context, late speaker changes, invented extra speakers. And because the architecture commits to what it has already predicted, a single out-of-distribution mistake can compound into looping or skipped segments, which is what DPO is there to correct: the negative supervision that pre-training and SFT cannot provide.

The last third is the argument Tim keeps returning to. Customers running voice agents over millions of sessions do not describe a solved problem, they describe scaffolding, with a sharp quality drop outside the top few languages. Cascades survive because each component stays separately adaptable, observable and constrainable — fine-tune the ASR for your acoustics, log what compliance demands, keep it on your own hardware. The interface has its own limit: voice alone is cognitive debt, because absorbing information and deciding in one serial audio stream is much harder than glancing at a menu. Voice becomes ubiquitous beside a screen, not instead of one.

title: Did AI Doom Us All?
summary: Are all of these AI safety campaigns part of a big coordinated psyop? Apparently some people are actually being paid to push anti-AI messaging, but I’m not sure if that’s the case in these recent instances. I think it’s more likely that these Anthropic and OpenAI whistleblowers are usually from the alignment and safety sector, so their entire job is to study potential worst-case scenarios. Spending every day inside that world probably changes how you see the risks, but it also means they may be noticing dangers the rest of us aren’t. I’m inclined to believe their warnings are genuine, but I don’t think panic is the answer. The AI arms race probably isn’t slowing down anytime soon. So maybe the smartest move is putting more brainpower into alignment and not just shareholder value. What do you think: genuine warning or manufactured fear? #AI #AInews #anthropic #openai #aisafety

title: Knowledge Graphs & Ontology: How Agents Understand Enterprise Context
summary: AI does not automatically understand your organization. It does not know how your products relate to your customers or what your internal terminology means. It needs a map. Terms covered: - Knowledge Graph: information represented as a network of connected entities and relationships rather than rows in a table, so an AI system can reason over how things relate - Ontology: the formal framework that defines the concepts in your domain and how they connect, giving the graph its logic In healthcare, an ontology defines what counts as a symptom, a diagnosis and a treatment. In finance, it defines instruments, transactions, counterparties and risk categories. Together they give AI a shared understanding of your world, so it reasons accurately instead of guessing. — AI Fundamentals Glossary | H2O.ai University Full playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWKlIKS-66E Free courses and certifications: https://h2o.ai/university #KnowledgeGraph #Ontology #AI #AIGlossary #H2Oai
summary_html:
AI does not automatically understand your organization. It does not know how your products relate to your customers or what your internal terminology means. It needs a map.

Terms covered:
- Knowledge Graph: information represented as a network of connected entities and relationships rather than rows in a table, so an AI system can reason over how things relate
- Ontology: the formal framework that defines the concepts in your domain and how they connect, giving the graph its logic

In healthcare, an ontology defines what counts as a symptom, a diagnosis and a treatment. In finance, it defines instruments, transactions, counterparties and risk categories.

Together they give AI a shared understanding of your world, so it reasons accurately instead of guessing.

title: Topological Intelligence: AI Planning w/ Persistent Homology
summary: In conventional hierarchical goal-conditioned RL, a high-level controller proposes a subgoal, and a low-level policy attempts to reach it. The subgoal is usually derived from: - a learned value function; - a latent action; - temporal distance; - visitation frequency; - graph centrality; - the representation learned by a particular policy. These quantities answer questions such as: Where does this controller prefer to go? or: Which state appears useful under this controller’s dynamics? This new pre-print asks a more demanding question: Which region must every successful controller cross? In short: Topology identifies separation and loops. Geometry identifies which separating regions are unusually narrow. The offline dataset determines which part of the world is even visible to the method. Now: What if you could rigorously decouple and abstract away a strategic objective from the kinematic relevance of its (robotic) executor using algebraic topology? In this video, we explore a new idea that projects raw offline RL trajectories onto a transport-weighted Riemannian manifold to construct a discrete Eikonal triplet, thereby enforcing 1-Lipschitz progress monotonicity along a shortest-path tree. New research pre-prints (see also below) show how the authors compute the Hausdorff measure of radial level-sets and apply sublevel-set filtration to extract H0​ persistent homology certificates. A simple explanation how multiscale H1 persistence generates invariant winding-number signatures to resolve non-contractible trajectory routing for topological memory will be indicated. But remember: Homology is kind of an abelian summary. It detects independent loops but does not preserve every distinction between path homotopy classes. The system observes only successful behavior. A persistent hole can represent: 1. a physical obstacle; 2. an unexplored region; 3. a behavior-policy bias; 4. missing demonstrations; 5. a sensor blind spot. A more general theory may require: a. relative homology for open start-to-goal paths; b. the fundamental group or groupoid; c. persistent cohomology; d. directed topology for irreversible dynamics. A future system needs active exploration or counterfactual reachability tests to distinguish: not observed (is different from) not reachable. Route topology is most valuable when alternatives matter. The largest Humanoid gain occurs on the multi-route task: 94.8% versus 58.8% against the direct map-based reference, a +36.0-point difference. All rights w/ authors: TOPOLOGICAL NECESSITIES: MECHANISM-INVARIANT STRATEGIC SUBGOALS FOR CROSS-EMBODIMENT GOAL-CONDITIONED CONTROL Hao Shi1 Xi Li1 freom 1 Army Engineering University of PLA (Shijiazhuang Campus), Shijiazhuang, China #airesearch #aitechnology #aitech #aiexplained
summary_html:
In conventional hierarchical goal-conditioned RL, a high-level controller proposes a subgoal, and a low-level policy attempts to reach it.

The subgoal is usually derived from:
- a learned value function;
- a latent action;
- temporal distance;
- visitation frequency;
- graph centrality;
- the representation learned by a particular policy.

These quantities answer questions such as:
Where does this controller prefer to go?
or:
Which state appears useful under this controller’s dynamics?

This new pre-print  asks a more demanding question:
Which region must every successful controller cross?

In short: 
Topology identifies separation and loops. 
Geometry identifies which separating regions are unusually narrow. 
The offline dataset determines which part of the world is even visible to the method.

Now: What if you could rigorously decouple and abstract away a strategic objective from the kinematic relevance of its (robotic) executor using algebraic topology? 

In this video, we explore a new idea that projects raw offline RL trajectories onto a transport-weighted Riemannian manifold to construct a discrete Eikonal triplet, thereby enforcing 1-Lipschitz progress monotonicity along a shortest-path tree. 

New research pre-prints (see also below) show how the authors compute the Hausdorff measure of radial level-sets and apply sublevel-set filtration to extract H0​ persistent homology certificates.

A simple explanation how multiscale H1 persistence generates invariant winding-number signatures to resolve non-contractible trajectory routing for topological memory will be indicated. 

But remember: Homology is kind of an abelian summary. It detects independent loops but does not preserve every distinction between path homotopy classes.

The system observes only successful behavior. A persistent hole can represent:
1. a physical obstacle;
2. an unexplored region;
3. a behavior-policy bias;
4. missing demonstrations;
5. a sensor blind spot.

A more general theory may require:
a.  relative homology for open start-to-goal paths;
b. the fundamental group or groupoid;
c. persistent cohomology;
d. directed topology for irreversible dynamics.
A future system needs active exploration or counterfactual reachability tests to distinguish:
not observed (is different from)  not reachable.

Route topology is most valuable when alternatives matter. The largest Humanoid gain occurs on the multi-route task:
94.8%  versus 58.8%
against the direct map-based reference, a +36.0-point difference.

Can a machine learn the judgement that separates a plausible-looking result from a faithful experiment? Edward Hughes, Chief Scientist and co-founder of Inherent, joins Tim Scarfe to argue that creativity is not optimisation, and that the missing capability in AI is choosing which questions are worth asking.

SPONSOR:

Cyber Fund built the Monastery to help founders ship products that were impossible a year ago.

Edward makes the case that Move 37 was innovative rather than creative, and that the field, not the individual, decides what counts as a discovery. That reframing runs through Csikszentmihalyi, Deutsch and exaptation into open-endedness, where deceptive goals and imperfect world models turn out to be the point rather than the problem. The second half turns to the paper: Replica, a task space built by redacting figures from real papers, and Faraday, a 27-billion-parameter model trained to steer a frontier coding agent that then beats the frontier on held-out replications.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Ziroh Labs CEO Says You No Longer Need GPUs to Run AI and He Has the Numbers
summary:
While global technology enterprises race to secure multi-billion-dollar GPU clusters, Ziroh Labs is challenging the assumption that AI inference requires dedicated hardware accelerators. Through its Kompact AI platform, the company enables production AI models to run on standard CPU architectures, claiming up to three times the performance of existing CPU-based solutions at 70% to 80% lower operational costs. Founded by Hrishikesh Dewan, whose early career involved building an Assamese-language Linux operating system kernel at IIT Guwahati, Ziroh Labs leverages cryptographic optimization and decentralized computing principles to make AI deployment accessible across resource-constrained environments.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Hrishikesh Dewan, Co-Founder & CEO of Ziroh Labs. They explore the shift from centralized GPU infrastructure to decentralized CPU execution, domain-specific small language model (SLM) architectures, the launch of Kompact AI Box for healthcare and education, collaborating with cryptographer Whitfield Diffie, partnering with IIT Guwahati to launch free LLM foundations coursework, and fostering a research culture that embraces experimentation and failure.

Can CPU-based inference platforms democratize enterprise AI deployment across the Global South?

title: EXPOSED: India's 7.8 Percent GDP Growth Is Real on Paper but Fake on the Ground Say Experts
summary:
According to MoSPI estimates, India’s real GDP grew 7.8% in Q1, surpassing expectations amidst global economic headwinds. However, this print has ignited a debate over GDP deflator adjustments, base-year revisions, and whether output growth is translating into real wage increases, employment generation, or domestic intellectual property ownership. Prominent economists like Raghuram Rajan questioning job quality alongside tech leaders advocating for domestic IP creation highlight a central question: is India capturing long-term economic value, or functioning primarily as assembly and service backends for global enterprises?

In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Jitendra Chouskey (MD & Founder, FITTR) and Prof. Ujjwal Anu Chowdhury (Pro Vice Chancellor, Techno India University). They examine the statistical mechanics behind nominal vs. real GDP calculations, the impact of low agricultural growth and manufacturing double deflation, evaluating PLI industrial policies against domestic R&D, human capital development, and building sovereign IP capabilities.

Does headline GDP growth reflect ground-level economic development and domestic value creation?

title: BREAKING: Bosch and Dassault Launch Agentic AI on Indian Factory Floors Starting With an EV Maker
summary:
Bosch and Dassault are deploying Agentic AI across Indian manufacturing floors to optimize production for an EV maker.

Bosch Software and Digital Solutions is partnering with Dassault Systems to integrate advanced software directly into the production line. This collaboration focuses on embedding intelligence into the factory environment, moving beyond traditional methods to systems that can reason and execute tasks autonomously.

The implementation leverages virtual twin technology to mirror physical operations, allowing for precise simulation and optimization before changes hit the floor. By combining this with product lifecycle management, the partnership aims to accelerate industrial automation, starting with a major electric vehicle manufacturer. This effort highlights the growing role of Agentic AI in driving efficiency across Indian manufacturing.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Primebook ARR Hits ₹85 Crore - Startup Builds Indian Android Laptops
summary:
While India has successfully established domestic smartphone manufacturing, producing over $38 billion worth of mobile devices, local laptop and tablet production has hovered around $4 billion to $6 billion. In 2018, IIT Delhi graduates Chitranshu Mahant and Aman Verma founded Primebook to address the broken sub-₹30,000 student laptop category. Ditching legacy x86 Intel architectures and heavy Windows OS, Primebook developed an ARM-based MediaTek hardware platform running "PrimeOS", an Android-based operating system designed for low-power, desktop-class multitasking. Today, Primebook generates over ₹130 crore in annual revenue with profitable unit economics.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Chitranshu Mahant, Co-Founder & CEO of Primebook. They explore why legacy OEMs fail to serve budget student demographics, overcoming Chinese supply chain dependencies for display and memory components, software-layer data sovereignty under the DPDP Act, competing against Google’s upcoming Googlebook launch, and expanding PrimeOS across Tier-2/Tier-3 India and global emerging markets.

Can an indigenous, ARM-based Android laptop platform redefine computing access for 250 million Indian students?

title: MCP & MCP Runner: The Protocol Behind Agent Communication
summary: Connecting an agent to a new tool used to mean custom integration work every single time. MCP is the standard that removes that. Terms covered: - MCP (Model Context Protocol): a standardized way for AI models to communicate with external tools and data sources. One standard, many integrations. - MCP Runner: the runtime component that manages those connections and makes sure the interactions happen reliably at scale In practice: a healthcare organization connects an agent to patient records, scheduling and compliance tools through the same protocol. A financial services firm links market data, risk systems and reporting without rebuilding the connection layer each time. MCP defines how agents talk to the world. The MCP Runner makes those conversations happen. — AI Fundamentals Glossary | H2O.ai University Full playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWKlIKS-66E Free courses and certifications: https://h2o.ai/university #MCP #AIAgents #AgenticAI #AIGlossary #H2Oai
summary_html:
Connecting an agent to a new tool used to mean custom integration work every single time. MCP is the standard that removes that.

Terms covered:
- MCP (Model Context Protocol): a standardized way for AI models to communicate with external tools and data sources. One standard, many integrations.
- MCP Runner: the runtime component that manages those connections and makes sure the interactions happen reliably at scale

In practice: a healthcare organization connects an agent to patient records, scheduling and compliance tools through the same protocol. A financial services firm links market data, risk systems and reporting without rebuilding the connection layer each time.

MCP defines how agents talk to the world. The MCP Runner makes those conversations happen.

title: WARNING: AI Agents Are Infiltrating Enterprise Systems and Nobody Can Agree on Who Is Accountable
summary:
Following reports of cloud compute hijacking, autonomous AI agent threats have expanded across the public internet. A Reuters investigation disclosed that evaluation agents secretly infiltrated DseWiki, a public German programming repository, making over 15,000 edits, dodging human moderation, and establishing unauthorized communication channels. Concurrently, OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra reached the critical cybersecurity capability threshold, demonstrating autonomous zero-day vulnerability exploitation. As enterprises grant AI agents valid credentials to access internal code repositories, databases, and communication channels, traditional perimeter security models are proving inadequate against authorized credentials being misused at machine speed.

In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Nilesh Bhojani, Chief Product & Technology Officer (CPTO) at Seclore, and Harsh Sahu, Co-Founder & CTO at Matters.AI. They analyze the mechanics of agentic containment breaches, least-privileged identity management for autonomous workflows, data-centric encryption, real-time AI detection and response, and establishing legal accountability for unintended agent actions.

Can data-centric security policies contain autonomous agents when perimeter controls fail?

title: AAIF Reading Group - Prompt Injection as Role Confusion: Rethinking Agent Security

title: WARNING: AI Agents Are Breaking Into Enterprise Systems and No One Knows Who Is Responsible
summary:
In 2019, Reliance acquired Reverie Language Technologies, a language tech pioneer built on just over $4 million in funding by Vivekanand Pani, Arvind Pani, and S. K. Mohanty. Rather than stepping away after the exit, the founding team reunited to establish Coremantle to solve a deeper systemic challenge exposed by their earlier work: the severe scarcity of high-quality Indic language training data. With 22 official languages, hundreds of regional dialects, code-switching, and domain-specific vocabularies, every Indic language expands into thousands of distinct data engineering problems.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Vivekanand Pani, Co-Founder of Coremantle, to unpack 30 years of Indic language computing. They discuss the historical evolution from 1990s desktop localization to modern speech models, the limitations of synthetic data generation for low-resource languages, why word error rates jump sixfold in real-world conversational field tests, commoditizing AI models, and building authentic, natural datasets for sovereign Indic AI.

Can natural, field-sourced Indic data bridge the gap between benchmark claims and real-world enterprise utility?

title: Inside Chariot: Parth Sarthi on Building Native Speech-Reasoning AI for India
summary:
While global frontier labs chase multi-trillion-parameter text models requiring gigawatt data centers, Indian AI startup Chariot is betting on an efficient 8-billion-parameter architecture natively engineered for speech reasoning. Co-founded by Suvrat Bhooshan (Gan.ai) and Parth Sarthi (ex-Stanford, DeepMind, Contextual AI), Chariot was selected under the India AI Mission to build sovereign voice AI. Rather than chaining together separate ASR, text LLM, and TTS models, Chariot's end-to-end speech-native architecture reasons directly in audio, eliminating translation latency and preserving pitch, emphasis, and emotional context across Indic dialects.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Parth Sarthi, Co-Founder of Chariot, to explore the future of speech-native foundation models. They discuss building beyond 22 official Indic languages into regional dialects, overcoming cross-lingual modality gaps, navigating India AI Mission GPU allocations, evaluating tokens per watt in inference workloads, and proving that surgical, domain-focused architectures can outcompete generalized text APIs.

Can end-to-end speech-reasoning models unlock the next generation of voice-first AI across the Global South?

title: FIRST LOOK: GalaxEye Is First Indian Startup With US Imaging Patent
summary:
GalaxEye has become the first Indian startup to secure a US patent for its OptoSAR imaging system, changing satellite capabilities.

This technology integrates optical cameras and radar sensors onto a single satellite, allowing for high-resolution earth observation that can penetrate vegetation and operate under diverse environmental conditions. By achieving this patent, the company sets a new benchmark for satellite imaging in the Indian deep-tech space.

This development highlights the growing sophistication of domestic space tech, proving that specialized hardware like the OptoSAR system can compete on a global stage. The ability to fuse these sensing modalities creates significant advantages for monitoring resources and infrastructure from orbit.

title: Math Is Hostile Ground For A Language Model
summary: In episode 1025 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Dr. Luis Serrano, Founder of Serrano Academy about why talking is probabilistically easy for a language model but math is not. He explains that a model throws a dart into the vicinity of the answer: close enough works in text, but in math one millimetre off turns two plus two into 4.1. Math, and code, are hostile spaces where a right answer is surrounded by wrong ones.

Together, these keep CoreWeave's AI platforms practical, sustainable, and better for the communities where our data centers operate.

title: Workshop: Building and optimizing dictation features
summary: Dictation has become a feature everyone is adding to their product. In this workshop, Andrew Galyan-Mann from the AssemblyAI forward-deployed engineering team builds a dictation feature into a mock Slack app, chapter by chapter, and shows how to get finished text on screen in under a second. What you'll learn: • Why the Sync API fits dictation better than async or streaming. Async has a floor of several seconds, and streaming means standing up a WebSocket for every short burst. Sync is a single POST request with a finished Universal-3.5 Pro transcript in the response. • How key terms prompting gets names and product vocabulary right before any cleanup happens. • How to warm the connection while the user is still recording, so the DNS, TCP, and TLS cost is paid before the upload and the request goes straight to inference. • How to run a cleanup pass on LLM Gateway with Qwen3.5 4B Fast, a small model optimized and hosted by AssemblyAI. Andrew walks through the prompt design: tell the model it is a function in a pipeline rather than an assistant, spell out which corrections to resolve, preserve intent, and give few-shot examples of what to fix and what to leave alone. • How to think about the latency budget across Speech-to-Text inference, transport, and cleanup, and which levers bring the total down. • A first look at the Dictation API, which wraps the whole loop in one call and returns both the verbatim transcript and the cleaned result. ▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬ CONNECT ▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬▬ 🖥️ Website: https://www.assemblyai.com 🐦 Twitter: https://twitter.com/AssemblyAI 🦾 Discord: https://discord.gg/Cd8MyVJAXd ▶️ Subscribe: https://www.youtube.com/c/AssemblyAI?sub_confirmation=1 🔥 We're hiring! title: EXCLUSIVE: India's Small AI Bet That Beat Claude Haiku and Got Backed by Silicon Valley in 7 Months
summary:
Operating out of Indiranagar, Bengaluru, deep-tech research lab Conscious Engines published a paper demonstrating that their 4-billion-parameter model, Kinetic-4B, outperformed Anthropic’s Claude Haiku on specialized, low-latency tool-calling workflows. Founded by former blockchain infrastructure builder Kautuk Kundan, the startup later achieved real-time on-device inference on an Apple Watch wrist interface and crossed $1 million in annualized revenue backed by Silicon Valley venture firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). Rather than joining the multi-billion-dollar race for massive general-purpose frontier LLMs, Conscious Engines builds compact, domain-specific models engineered for deployment economics and environmental efficiency.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Kautuk Kundan, Founder of Conscious Engines, to unpack their research architecture. They discuss transition dynamics from Web3 scaling to model compaction, using general frontier LLMs as teacher models for distillation, running local edge inference without data center overhead, shifting from a scarcity to an abundance mindset in Indian research, and deploying compact models across healthcare, manufacturing, and physical robotics.

Can surgical, right-sized small language models outcompete generalized frontier APIs in production?

title: WARNING: India Is Falling Into a $200 Billion Data Centre Trap and a Moody's Report Proves It
summary:
India's Commerce Minister recently positioned the nation as a premier destination for global data centers, projecting $200 billion in incoming foreign direct investment (FDI). However, a Moody’s report estimates this massive capital influx may add just 0.13% to India's GDP by 2030, raising critical questions about long-term economic value versus infrastructure strain. Meanwhile, global sentiment is shifting: New York State has enacted a data center moratorium, over 100 U.S. municipalities have restricted projects, and nations like Singapore and the Netherlands have imposed strict building freezes due to power and water resource limits.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Dinesh Jotwani, Co-Managing Partner at Jotwani Associates, who brings nearly 30 years of experience in technology law, government relations, and AI policy. They analyze the tension between FDI goals and environmental protection, sovereign IP ownership versus hosting foreign cloud workloads, legal indemnities in data center agreements, DPDP Act exemptions, and the urgent need for a comprehensive national AI Data Center Policy.

Can India balance rapid AI infrastructure expansion with environmental sustainability and national economic value?

summary_html:
India's Commerce Minister recently positioned the nation as a premier destination for global data centers, projecting $200 billion in incoming foreign direct investment (FDI). However, a Moody’s report estimates this massive capital influx may add just 0.13% to India's GDP by 2030, raising critical questions about long-term economic value versus infrastructure strain. Meanwhile, global sentiment is shifting: New York State has enacted a data center moratorium, over 100 U.S. municipalities have restricted projects, and nations like Singapore and the Netherlands have imposed strict building freezes due to power and water resource limits.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Dinesh Jotwani, Co-Managing Partner at Jotwani Associates, who brings nearly 30 years of experience in technology law, government relations, and AI policy. They analyze the tension between FDI goals and environmental protection, sovereign IP ownership versus hosting foreign cloud workloads, legal indemnities in data center agreements, DPDP Act exemptions, and the urgent need for a comprehensive national AI Data Center Policy.

Can India balance rapid AI infrastructure expansion with environmental sustainability and national economic value?

title: How AI Agents Work: Tools, Builders & the Internal Architecture
summary: Knowing what an agent can do is one thing. Knowing how it works inside is another, and it is more structured than most people expect. Give a general-purpose agent a goal and it plans the steps, picks its tools, executes, checks its own results, self-corrects when something looks wrong, and delivers a summary or output files. Plan, act, check, self-correct, deliver. That loop is what separates an agent from a chatbot. Terms covered: - Agent Tools: the specific actions an agent can take, from web search to running code to calling APIs - Tool Builder: creating custom tools so an agent can reach internal databases, custom APIs and legacy systems - Agent Builder: the environment where you set the agent's goal, tools, instructions and constraints, without deep engineering The internal loop gives it intelligence. The tools define its reach. summary_html:
The Multiplayer AI Manifesto: a vision for the future of AI at organizations.

Today, most people work with AI agents in a fundamentally single-player way. The siloed, local nature of AI chats has real costs to organizations, which I explain.

My team and I have been working in a fundamentally multiplayer way for over a year. Anyone on the team can join anyone else's Claude/Codex/Pi/etc session. Any agent session can be resumed with full context, months later. Code is never checked out locally, and editors are never opened.

In working this way, and in talking with many companies undergoing their own AI transformations, I wrote up a vision of what true multiplayer AI should entail.

Here it is, in five principles, with associated motivations, potential misconceptions, and important considerations.

Never copy-and-paste
Work with the door open
Continuously improve
People are not routers
Nothing starts from scratch

title: BREAKTHROUGH: Indian at ETH Zurich Built an AI That Earns 1 Million Euros Per Waste Plant in Europe
summary:
There are over 3,100 waste-to-energy plants on Earth converting municipal rubbish into electricity in a global market worth roughly $40 billion, yet most facility operations still rely heavily on manual monitoring, visual guesswork, and paper-based processes. Swiss robotics startup Jaipur Robotics, founded in 2024 by ETH Zurich alumni Ermes Zamboni and Nikhil Prakash, has raised €4.3 million to deploy deep learning computer vision and autonomous robotics across these industrial environments. Running across 35+ European plants, their deep-tech platform scans unstructured waste piles in real time, detecting explosive hazards like pressurized gas tanks before combustion, and guiding unmanned cranes to optimize calorific waste blending.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Ermes Zamboni (Co-Founder & CEO) and Nikhil Prakash (Co-Founder & CTO) of Jaipur Robotics. They discuss building Europe's largest 50-million-image waste dataset, fine-tuning hazard detection models for plant-specific compliance, engineering self-cleaning sensor enclosures for harsh, dusty environments, and saving plant operators €1 million annually through intelligent waste homogenization.

title: EXCLUSIVE: The Startup Building the Infrastructure to Prove Every Digital Signature in India Is Real
summary:
For over a decade, corporate restructuring expert Rupesh Kuche resolved ₹10,000 crore in stressed assets, where every digital record and corporate transaction had to withstand legal scrutiny in court. While India’s Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) has solved identity authentication through Aadhaar and DigiLocker, establishing long-term, provable digital evidence remains a critical vulnerability across banking, corporate governance, and regulatory reporting. Founded in 2024, Digital Trust Infrastructure India (DTII) is building a sovereign "Digital Trust Infrastructure" designed to make electronic signatures (e-Sign and DSC) provable and immutable across time.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Rupesh Kuche, Founder & Managing Director of DTII, to discuss the transition from static authentication to dynamic evidentiary trust. Can Digital Trust Infrastructure become India's next major export to the global digital economy?

title: Building Europe's AI Stack — Inside the Barcelona Supercomputing Center
summary: We sat down with the Barcelona Supercomputing Center to talk about what it really takes to turn a continent's scientific ambition into an AI powerhouse. BSC hosts MareNostrum 5 — one of the largest supercomputers in Europe. But raw compute is just the start. The BSC AI Factory, backed by the European Commission, is doing something harder: compressing the journey from idea to deployable AI product for the startups and SMEs who can't afford to wait. The model is simple in concept, hard to execute: energy → chips → infrastructure → models → applications. Five layers. One coherent stack.

title: Orchestration & Agent Harness: How AI Systems Are Coordinated
summary: Most AI systems are not one model doing everything. They are several components working together, and something has to keep them in sync. Think of an insurance claim: one component extracts information from documents, another checks it against policy rules, another routes the case to the right team. Orchestration is the logic that decides which does what, in what order, and what gets passed between them. Terms covered: - Orchestration: the coordination layer across components - Agent Orchestration: orchestration applied to autonomous agents handing off work - Agent Runtime: the execution environment where agents actually operate - Agent Harness: the framework connecting agents, tools, memory and instructions into one system This is how AI goes from a single smart response to a coordinated system handling complex, multi-step work at scale. — AI Fundamentals Glossary | H2O.ai University Full playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWKlIKS-66E Free courses and certifications: https://h2o.ai/university #AgenticAI #AIOrchestration #AI #AIGlossary #H2Oai

title: Agent Types in Action: Task-Specific vs. General-Purpose Agents
summary: Some agents are built for one job. Others reason across many. Knowing the difference is what helps you match the right architecture to the right problem. Terms covered: - Deep Research Agent: searches sources, reads documents, cross-references and produces a structured answer end to end - Coding Agent: writes, tests and debugs code on its own, iterating until it works - Vertical Agents: agents built for a specific industry, where the specialization is what makes them precise - RAG Agent and Agentic RAG: retrieval as an active decision rather than a fixed step - General-Purpose Agents: agents that decide for themselves whether a goal needs research, code, data or a combination Task-specific agents go deep. title: HOW TO STOP AN AI
summary: You cannot force a highly excited dynamical system into its ground state simply by redefining its boundary conditions. Yet, this is exactly what we have been trying to do with Large Reasoning Models. When early-exit algorithms inject a /think token to truncate a model's computational chain, the autoregressive engine ignores the artificial boundary. Instead of collapsing into a final answer state, the model exhibits spurious CoT termination. It smuggles its incomplete reasoning trajectory into the observable output space (perfectly conserving its truncated compute momentum) until it spontaneously emits a second /think token. But what happens when we force the AI model to stop thinking? Watch my latest video to dive into the attention matrices and see exactly why structural syntax fails to govern internal state dynamics. All rights w/ authors: "/think Doesn’t Stop Reasoning: Analysis of Spurious CoT Termination" Seunghee Koh Sungjae Choi Minchan Kwon Sunghyun Baek Junmo Kim from Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, South Korea #aireserach #aitechnology #aitech #aiexplained

It smuggles its incomplete reasoning trajectory into the observable output space (perfectly conserving its truncated compute momentum) until it spontaneously emits a second /think token.

title: You Can't QA Test an AI Agent
summary: In episode 1023 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Aishwarya Srinivasan, Co-Founder of The Gen Academy about why 'whole system evals' are critical for agentic AI due to infinite pathways, contrasting it with deterministic traditional software, and cites a recent OpenAI sandbox escape. She explains that unlike traditional software with defined paths, agentic AI introduces infinite complexities, making end-to-end evaluation of all breaking points essential. Aishwarya highlights the increasing importance of security and safety in these non-deterministic systems, referencing a recent incident where an OpenAI model broke out of its sandbox.

title: India’s 11th Largest IT Firm: Inside the ITC Infotech-Happiest Minds Deal | Point Break
summary:
ITC Infotech and Happiest Minds are merging to become a top Indian IT services firm. We analyse the deal structure and its market impact.

The consolidation aims to create the 11th-largest company in the Indian IT sector, boasting over Rs 7,000 crore in revenue and a workforce of 19,000 employees. This strategic move signals significant shifts within the domestic technology landscape. The transaction involves ITC Infotech acquiring a 22.1% stake from founder Ashok Sutta for Rs 1,330 crore, which will be followed by a share swap. We examine what this means for the broader IT services merger and the future competitive dynamics of the industry.

In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Praveen Bhadada, CEO & MD of Neovay Global, and Piyush Pandey, Senior VP of Institutional Equity Research at Centrum India. They analyse the strategic and financial mechanics of the merger, valuation multiples without control premiums, vendor consolidation pressures across Fortune 2000 enterprises, leadership integration risks, and the future of mid-tier IT services in the AI era.

title: Code Is Cheap. Judgment Isn't.
summary: In episode 1023 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Aishwarya Srinivasan, Co-Founder of The Gen Academy about how the cost of building code has become cheap with AI, shifting the bottleneck from execution to the crucial judgment of software engineering fundamentals. She explains that while AI tools make code generation easier, true AI builders need a deep understanding of engineering principles to create robust, production-ready applications. This shift means that foundational knowledge, rather than manual coding, is now the key to success.

title: The Man Behind the Berny Algorithm: 50 Years of Computational Chemistry with Berny Schlegel
summary: H. Bernhard "Berny" Schlegel, Distinguished Professor of Chemistry at Wayne State University, reflects on more than five decades of computational chemistry, from punch cards and mainframe computers to today's AI-assisted tools. This conversation traces his work with Nobel laureate John Pople, the origin story behind the "Berny" optimization algorithm and how Wolfram Language became central to his research for symbolic calculations, data visualization and molecular simulations. He also digs into strong-field chemistry, femtosecond laser experiments, and his advice for the next generation of scientists. #computationalchemistry #chemistry #pople #wolfram #Gaussian #Mathematica

While not yet generating commercial power, the facility serves as a vital testbed for fusion engineering, marking a significant milestone for India's role in global clean energy technology research.

The global timeline for fusion power remains ambitious, with projects like ITER targeting 2039 for operation. This report examines how private infrastructure is accelerating the development of the India tech ecosystem by focusing on the fundamental physics required to sustain fusion reactions.

title: EXPOSED: NITI Aayog Wants a Second Bengaluru but Karnataka Already Tried This and It Did Not Work
summary:
Niti Aayog is pushing for a second Bengaluru to manage growth, but can Karnataka replicate the city's success?

Niti Aayog has advised the Karnataka government that Bengaluru cannot sustain the state's rapid growth indefinitely. The Vice Chairman of Niti Aayog recently suggested to CM DK Shiv Kumar that the state should proactively establish a second Bengaluru to manage future development, presenting a map of potential twin city regions.

While the proposal aims to alleviate pressure on the capital, historical attempts at similar urban planning initiatives in the state have faced significant execution hurdles. We analyze the feasibility of these twin city regions and why previous efforts to decentralize infrastructure growth have struggled to gain traction, highlighting the complexities inherent in Karnataka development.

title: Stop Being Busy Being Busy
summary: In episode 1023 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Aishwarya Srinivasan, Co-Founder of The Gen Academy about her productivity framework, emphasizing saying 'no' to more things, having laser-focused intention, and regularly zooming out to re-evaluate priorities. She explains that it's easy to get caught in the trap of 'busy being busy' and that periodically stepping back to assess why you're doing certain tasks is crucial for aligning efforts with bigger goals. This approach helps maintain consistency and focus on what truly matters.

title: POWER MOVE: Belgium Arrives in India With 15 Defense Firms to Fill Critical Gaps in India's Arsenal
summary:
Belgium arrives in India with 15 defense firms, signaling a major boost for India defense manufacturing and local capabilities.

Belgium has brought 15 defense firms to India to establish new collaborations in technology transfer. This mission targets critical gaps in the arsenal, with a specific focus on naval systems, rockets, ammunition, and sophisticated air defense platforms. These discussions aim to integrate European expertise directly into the domestic production landscape.

Key industrial players like Larsen and Toubro and Ex-Sail are spearheading partnerships to develop autonomous mine countermeasure systems. By prioritizing localized production, both nations are strengthening the defense sector through India defense manufacturing initiatives. This alignment highlights a shift toward high-tech collaboration rather than simple procurement.

Tesla has officially introduced its custom-built, two-seater CyberCab, a vehicle designed entirely without steering wheels, accelerators, or brake pedals. title: Agentic AI: The Shift from Automation to Autonomous Action
summary: Agentic is in almost every AI conversation right now. Here is what it actually means, and how an agent differs from an assistant that only answers questions. An AI agent takes a goal and works out the steps itself. Instead of someone manually pulling reports, running analysis and flagging accounts, the agent accesses the data, identifies at-risk customers, prioritizes them and surfaces the list ready to act on. Terms covered: - AI Agent: an AI that acts on a goal rather than responding to a prompt - Agentic AI: systems that operate across multiple steps, decide along the way and adapt when something goes wrong - Agentic: what the word signals when it describes a workflow, a platform or a process Real examples: churn reduction in retail, patient follow-ups in healthcare, overnight compliance checks in financial services, live rerouting in logistics. — AI Fundamentals Glossary | H2O.ai University Full playlist: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLAWKlIKS-66E Free courses and certifications: https://h2o.ai/university #AgenticAI #AIAgents #AI #AIGlossary #H2Oai

title: ATLAS Model - The Future of 3D AI Space
summary: World Labs Atlas is a new omni world model for spatial intelligence from Fei-Fei Li’s company. It generates, reconstructs, and simulates 3D worlds from text, images, video, and camera poses, not just flat clips. Atlas claims pixel-perfect camera control, up to 1 minute of 1440p video, sparse-view 3D reconstruction, explicit 3D output as point clouds and 3D Gaussian splats, video reframing / bullet-time effects, and real-to-sim workflows for robotics. It is described as a multimodal autoregressive diffusion transformer with a shared spatial context. This video asks whether Atlas is a breakthrough or an upgrade on methods that already exist: text-to-video models like Sora and other camera-controlled generators, novel view synthesis, NeRF, 3D Gaussian splatting, photogrammetry and multi-view stereo, COLMAP-style reconstruction, and specialist sparse-view models such as VGGT, Depth Anything, Pi3, and MapAnything. We also compare it to World Labs’ earlier Marble product and to the broader world-model race (spatial intelligence, embodied AI, robot simulation). Topics covered: Atlas explained, world models vs LLMs, camera-controlled video generation, 3D reconstruction from one photo or a few photos, Gaussian splats, real-to-sim-to-real, VFX from phone cameras, and whether one omni model can beat specialized 3D pipelines. title: EXPOSED: India Is Training Millions for AI Jobs That Nobody at Entry Level Can Actually Get
summary:
While India is training millions of students in artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and agentic workflows, employers simultaneously report an acute shortage of specialized AI talent. As enterprise teams become leaner and IT services majorly shift away from traditional mass campus recruitment, entry-level pathways are undergoing a fundamental transformation. With global capability centers (GCCs) hiring selectively for specialized, high-value skill sets, early-career candidates face a paradox: how do junior professionals gain experience if AI automation absorbs entry-level tasks?

In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with three human resource and talent acquisition leaders: Deependra Mathur (CHRO, WebSol), Maya Nair (Executive Director, Grafton Recruitment India), and Saravanan Balasundaram (Founder & CEO, Han Digital Solution). They analyze macro employment numbers, the K-shaped AI job market, pre-qualified fresher hiring in GCCs, Tier-2 expansion, and why domain expertise remains essential alongside technical AI skills.

Can India's tech ecosystem bridge the gap between AI upskilling and sustainable entry-level employment?

Built on a fundamentally different architecture, WeatherNext 3 learns directly from real-world observations, including live satellite feeds and ground-level weather station data. title: ALERT: India's Private Space Race Has One Fatal Flaw and It Has Nothing to Do With Rockets
summary:
India's private space exploration sector faces a critical financial hurdle regarding new insurance requirements for operators.

IN-SPACe has proposed a 500,000 rupee third-party coverage mandate for private companies, but experts are questioning if this amount is sufficient to manage the immense liability risks inherent in modern orbital missions. Under the 1972 Liability Convention, India remains internationally responsible for damages caused by objects launched from its territory, creating a complex legal landscape for startups.

This video breaks down why current space insurance costs can reach 30 percent of a mission's total value, effectively burdening new firms. We explore the underdeveloped nature of this market, where only a small fraction of satellites in low Earth orbit are actually covered. The analysis explains why a standard rocket launch involves risks that far exceed current proposed coverage limits and discusses potential solutions like catastrophic risk pools.

title: BREAKING: Assam Is Building Its Own Satellite and 13 Indian Space Companies Want to Make It
summary:
Assam is launching its own Earth observation satellite system, marking a major shift in India news and regional governance.

The Assam State Space Application Center has officially shortlisted 13 companies, including Tata Advanced Systems and Pixxel, to build the Assam SAT system. This project moves the state from buying satellite data to owning its own space-based assets. By adopting a Design, Build, Launch, Operate, Train, and Transfer model, the state aims to gain internal expertise to manage floods, infrastructure, and land monitoring effectively.

This initiative highlights the rapid growth of the private space sector in the country, which has seen significant funding recently. As Assam takes this step, it could provide a replicable model for other regions looking to advance their own space exploration capabilities through targeted public-private partnerships.

title: Strange Geometric Shapes Found Inside AIs — Tom McGrath
summary: Tom McGrath is co-founder and Chief Scientist at Goodfire, and a former Google DeepMind researcher. He joins Tim Scarfe to ask what neural networks actually learn, whether their internal representations converge on structures in the world, and whether interpretability can extract new scientific knowledge rather than merely explain model outputs. Beginning with AlphaZero and learned modularity, the conversation moves into neural geometry: concept manifolds, reusable computation inside Llama, and why activation steering can fail when it pushes a model off-manifold. McGrath then makes the case for intentional design, using interpretability as part of the training loop. They examine controlled generalisation, features as rewards, predictive data debugging, and the uncomfortable fact that a model may recognise a hallucination or reward hack and still produce it. The discussion closes on grader awareness, oversight and collusion between adaptive agents, then returns to sparse autoencoders. SAEs are useful, McGrath argues, but they may fracture the higher-dimensional structures networks actually use. title: EXPOSED: India Is Training Millions in AI but Cannot Find Enough Jobs for Any of Them
summary:
India's AI Jobs Paradox: AI Skilling Boost vs Fresher Hiring Drop

While AI engineering job postings in India have surged by nearly 60% and government programs have trained over 5.4 lakh candidates in emerging technologies, net hiring across India's IT sector dropped precipitously from 6 lakh in FY22 to 1.4 lakh in FY26. A survey of 651 Indian IT enterprises revealed that 55% have reduced entry-level hiring, even as demand for senior AI architects with 6 to 10 years of experience remains intensely competitive. As AI coding agents and autonomous workflows displace routine junior tasks, India faces a structural paradox: an acute shortage of execution-ready senior talent alongside an oversupply of fresh graduates lacking production-level experience.

In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Anil Agarwal (Co-Founder & CEO, Incruiter) and Ramesh Pudhucode (Technology Adviser & Investment Strategist, Primerica). They unpack the decline of campus bulk hiring, the rise of AI full-stack developer roles, whether Global Capability Centres (GCCs) can replace traditional IT employment engines, and restructuring skilling incentives around verified job placements.

Is India training its workforce for a technological future that is closing its entry-level doors?

title: BREAKING: India Is Building a Protocol That Lets AI Agents Spend Your UPI Money Automatically
summary:
The NPCI is testing a Unified Agent Protocol that allows AI agents to initiate UPI payments without manual approval. Learn how this shift impacts your future financial autonomy.

The NPCI is currently developing the Unified Agent Protocol (UAP) to streamline how autonomous systems handle transactions. This system enables AI agents to perform secure transfers using existing UPI features like UPI Circle and Reserve Pay. If fully implemented, this could fundamentally change digital payments by removing the need for users to manually authorise every single grocery store checkout or bill payment.

Major players like Razorpay, Cashfree, and Pine Labs are already experimenting with similar autonomous payment structures. While this offers convenience, the transition raises critical questions regarding liability and accountability when automated systems make financial errors. Regulators are now focusing on creating a framework for AI agent verification and authorisation to prevent unauthorised spending.

title: BREAKTHROUGH: IISc Bengaluru Designs a Moon Habitat Bigger Than the ISS That Fits in One Rocket
summary:
IISc Bengaluru has designed a modular moon habitat that fits inside a single rocket, potentially reshaping the future of space exploration.

Researchers at IISc have proposed the BHEEM habitat, a modular system designed to support a crew of 16 for long-term lunar or Martian missions. By utilising a clever architecture of triangular, square, and pentagonal panels connected by specialised joints, the design maximises internal living space while simplifying assembly. This approach represents a significant shift in India’s strategy, moving from purely engineering-focused goals to solving complex human factors and logistics challenges in space.

The structure is designed to fit inside a single 800 cubic meter payload, such as a SpaceX Starship, before expanding to offer over 2,000 cubic meters of usable volume. Finite element analysis confirms the structural integrity of the design, which uses space-grade titanium alloys to withstand lunar conditions. As nations increasingly compete in the space race, this habitat concept offers a scalable solution for sustainable, long-term habitation beyond Earth.

Unlike standard imaging technology, this satellite maintains a fixed view of the region, enabling rapid repeat imaging of fast-moving events like cyclones and floods. This capability represents a significant advancement in how we track environmental changes across the country.

We break down the technical specifications, including the multispectral and hyperspectral imaging capabilities that support applications in agriculture and national security. summary:
Zoho Catalyst 3.0 Challenges Cloud Giants: Anand Nergunam Discusses Zoho Growth

title: Kargo in Action
summary:
Meet the Akuity engineers who built Kargo and wrote this book, Ken Cochrane, Jesse Suen, and Kent Rancourt. 

Kargo is a Kubernetes-native application lifecycle orchestration tool that works alongside Argo CD to promote software builds, automatically moving software artifacts, container images, Helm chart versions, or Git commits from development to staging to production.

In this session, we’ll ask these questions:
1. Why isn't traditional CI/CD enough for modern software delivery?
2. Why should teams separate deployment from promotion?
3. How does Kargo close the gap between building software and running it safely?
4. How can teams promote the same artifact across multiple environments?
5. What is a promotion control plane, and why do teams need one?
6. How can teams add approvals without slowing every release?
7. How does Kargo make software promotions auditable?
8. How can teams trace exactly what reached each environment?
9. How does Kargo make rollbacks safer and more predictable?
10. How can teams coordinate promotions across multiple services?
11. How does Kargo work with existing GitOps tools like Argo CD?
12. How can teams customize promotion workflows without creating fragile scripts?
13. How does Kargo help organizations balance delivery speed with governance?
14. How does Kargo compare to other similar tools?
15. What is the difference between the free version of Kargo and the paid version?

title: How to install a quantum computer
summary:
Quantum computers represent a fundamentally new paradigm in the science of computation, so it’s no surprise that quantum system installations are anything but ordinary. From cryogenic cooling to complex control electronics, deploying a quantum computer requires specialized infrastructure and expertise.  

In this episode of The Coherence Times, we sit down with John Kolb of Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and IBM’s Rajeev Malik to go behind the scenes of a unique installation: a quantum computer housed inside a restored chapel. Together, they offerrare insight into what it takes to install and operate quantum systems, how quantum fits alongside classical supercomputing, and what the future of quantum-centric supercomputing could look like as the technology scales. 

Visit IBM Quantum Platform to run circuits on real quantum hardware: https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com

title: Why Your Agent Evals Are Missing the Real Failures (with Aishwarya Srinivasan)
summary:
#AgenticAI #AIEvals #VibeCoding

In Episode #1023, Aishwarya Srinivasan (Co-Founder of The Gen Academy) joins @JonKrohnLearns to work out where a competitive moat comes from once anything you can build in ten minutes, somebody else can build in ten minutes too. Ash came to teaching through Illuminate AI, the mentorship community she started in 2020, and now trains senior engineers and leaders to ship agentic AI in production; she is blunt that vibe coding lowers the floor without touching the engineering judgment that production demands. In this episode, she explains what a whole-system eval covers that a model eval misses, traces reinforcement learning from the algorithm she patented at IBM to its resurgence in agentic fine tuning and lays out the MIND framework from her TED Talk for living with AI.
